examples.ko: 저는 저녁마다 시트콤을 한 편씩 봐요.
examples.en: I watch one sitcom episode every evening.

examples.ko: 이 시트콤은 가족 이야기라서 온 가족이 같이 봐요.
examples.en: This sitcom is about a family, so the whole family watches it together.

examples.ko: 주인공이 너무 웃겨서 시트콤을 보다가 배를 잡고 웃었어요.
examples.en: The main character was so funny that I held my stomach laughing while watching the sitcom.
What is a popular sitcom these days?

examples.ko: 한국어를 배우려고 시트콤으로 일상 대화를 들어요.
examples.en: I listen to everyday conversation through sitcoms to learn Korean.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 보던 시트콤이 다시 방송되고 있어요!
examples.en: The sitcom I used to watch as a kid is being broadcast again!

explain: 시트콤은 같은 인물들이 나오는 일상 이야기를 웃기게 그린 드라마예요. 짧은 코너로 나뉘는 개그 프로그램과 달라요. 일상 대화가 많아서 한국어 듣기 공부 자료로 자주 추천해요.
explain_en: A sitcom is a comedy drama about the everyday life of the same set of characters. It differs from a gag show, which is split into short sketches. It is full of daily conversation, so it is often recommended for listening practice.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 기다리는 동안 마음이 심란해요.
examples.en: My mind is unsettled while waiting for the exam results.

examples.ko: 회사 일 때문에 요즘 머리가 심란했어요.
examples.en: My head has been in a mess lately because of work.

examples.ko: 심란한 표정으로 앉아 있는 친구를 위로해 줬어요.
examples.en: I comforted my friend who was sitting there looking troubled.

examples.ko: 이사 날짜가 다가오니까 마음이 심란해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: With the moving date approaching, I felt so uneasy that I couldn't sleep.
After watching the news, I felt even more troubled.
When my mind is unsettled, I take a walk.

explain: '속상하다'는 일이 마음에 안 들어서 상한 느낌이고, '심란하다'는 걱정과 생각이 많아서 마음이 어수선한 느낌이에요. 주로 '마음이 심란하다', '머리가 심란하다'로 써요. 표준 발음은 [심난]이에요.
explain_en: 속상하다 is feeling hurt because something went badly, while 심란하다 is feeling scattered because of too many worries and thoughts. It usually appears as 마음이 심란하다 or 머리가 심란하다. The standard pronunciation is [심난].

examples.en: My younger sibling dressed up nicely to go to the party.
At Christmas, we decorate the living room with sparkling ornaments.

examples.ko: 치장하는 데 시간이 너무 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes too long to get dolled up.
Grandmother came out beautifully dressed in a hanbok.

examples.ko: 저는 화려하게 치장하는 것보다 편한 옷이 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer comfortable clothes to dressing up flashily.
I will decorate the front of the shop with flowers.

explain: '꾸미다'가 사람과 물건 모두에 두루 쓰이는 말이라면, '치장하다'는 겉모습을 화려하게 꾸밀 때 써요. 때로는 속은 비어 있는데 겉만 꾸민다는 느낌이 있어요. '화장하다'는 얼굴만 꾸미지만 치장은 옷과 장신구까지 포함해요.
explain_en: 꾸미다 is a general word for decorating people or things, while 치장하다 stresses making the outward look showy. It can carry a feeling that only the surface is dressed up. 화장하다 is about the face only, but 치장하다 includes clothes and accessories.

examples.en: I saw a huge rhinoceros at the zoo.
A rhinoceros has its horn on top of its nose.
Many wild rhinoceroses live in Africa.
The child drew a rhinoceros and showed it off.

examples.ko: 코뿔소처럼 힘이 센 사람이 되고 싶어요!
examples.en: I want to be strong like a rhinoceros!

examples.ko: 사냥 때문에 코뿔소의 수가 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: The number of rhinoceroses has dropped a lot because of hunting.

explain: '코'와 '뿔'이 합쳐진 말로 코 위의 뿔을 그대로 이름에 담았어요. 옛 이름 '무소'도 있지만 일상에서는 '코뿔소'를 훨씬 많이 써요. 발음은 [코뿔쏘]처럼 'ㅅ'이 세게 나요.
explain_en: The word joins 코 (nose) and 뿔 (horn), so the name describes the animal directly. There is also an older word 무소, but 코뿔소 is far more common in daily life. The 소 is pronounced with a tense sound, like [코뿔쏘].

examples.ko: 나뭇가지에 파랑새 한 마리가 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A bluebird is sitting on the branch.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 파랑새 동화책을 읽은 적이 있어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I read a bluebird storybook.
They say the bluebird symbolizes happiness.
I heard a bluebird singing outside the window.

examples.ko: 행복은 멀리 있는 파랑새가 아니라 가까이에 있어요.
examples.en: Happiness is not a faraway bluebird; it is close by.
I bought a bluebird-shaped key ring.

explain: '파랑새'는 실제 새 이름이기도 하지만 한국에서는 '행복'을 뜻하는 상징으로 더 자주 써요. 이야기에서 '행복은 가까이에 있다'는 주제와 함께 많이 나와요. 새를 세는 말은 '마리'예요.
explain_en: 파랑새 is a real bird, but in Korea it is more often used as a symbol of happiness. It often appears with the theme that happiness is close at hand. Birds are counted with 마리.

examples.ko: 한옥 지붕에는 검은 기와가 올려져 있어요.
examples.en: Black roof tiles are laid on the roof of a hanok.
They replaced the roof tiles of the old temple with new ones.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 기와 위로 빗물이 흘러내려요.
examples.en: When it rains, rainwater runs down over the roof tiles.
I looked around a village lined with tile-roofed houses.
A few roof tiles broke in the typhoon.
I got a tile-shaped snack as a gift!

explain: 한국의 전통 집인 한옥은 지붕이 기와인지 초가인지로 나눠요. 기와로 지붕을 얹은 집은 '기와집', 짚으로 덮은 집은 '초가집'이라고 불러요. 기와는 낱장을 '장'으로 세어요.
explain_en: Traditional Korean houses (한옥) are often divided by their roof: 기와 or straw thatch. A house with a tile roof is a 기와집, and one with a straw roof is a 초가집. Individual tiles are counted with 장.

examples.en: When night fell, the neon lights on the street came on.
Myeongdong is full of flashy neon lights.
We made the shop name into a neon sign.
I took a photo under the neon lights.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 네온이 길에 비쳐서 예뻐요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the neon reflects on the road and looks pretty.

examples.ko: 저 가게 네온은 고장 났는지 깜빡거려요.
examples.en: The neon at that shop is flickering, maybe because it's broken.

explain: '네온'은 원래 기체 이름이지만 일상에서는 밤거리의 네온 불빛이나 간판을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 보통 '네온사인', '네온 간판'으로 더 자주 말해요. 불이 '켜지다', '꺼지다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: 네온 is originally the name of a gas, but in daily speech it usually means the glowing lights or signs seen on night streets. People more often say 네온사인 or 네온 간판. It goes with 켜지다 and 꺼지다.

examples.ko: 지진이 나면 가까운 대피소로 가야 해요.
examples.en: If an earthquake happens, you must go to the nearest shelter.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 대피소 위치를 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked where the shelter in our neighborhood is.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 주민들이 대피소에서 하룻밤을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The residents spent a night at the shelter because of the typhoon.
Water and blankets were prepared at the shelter.
I heard that this subway station is used as a shelter.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀라지 않게 대피소까지 손을 잡고 갔어요.
examples.en: We held hands all the way to the shelter so the children wouldn't be scared.

explain: '대피소'는 재난이 났을 때 잠깐 몸을 피하는 곳이에요. 오래 지내는 '임시 주거지'와는 달라요. 안내 방송에서는 '대피소로 이동하세요'처럼 자주 들려요.
explain_en: A 대피소 is a place to take cover briefly when a disaster strikes, different from longer-term temporary housing. In emergency announcements you often hear 대피소로 이동하세요. It is the destination you head to right away.

examples.en: In spring, I bought tomato seedlings at the market.
I transplanted the seedlings into a pot.

examples.ko: 아버지는 텃밭에 상추 모종을 심고 계세요.
examples.en: My father is planting lettuce seedlings in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 모종이 시들지 않게 물을 자주 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to water often so the seedlings don't wilt.
I picked out a few seedlings at the flower shop.
The seedlings grew and bore fruit!

explain: '씨앗'은 아직 심기 전의 것이고, '모종'은 씨앗에서 싹이 터서 옮겨 심을 만큼 자란 어린 식물이에요. 보통 '모종을 사다', '모종을 심다'로 말해요. 텃밭이나 베란다 키우기에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: A 씨앗 is a seed before planting, while a 모종 is a young plant that has already sprouted and is ready to be transplanted. People say 모종을 사다 or 모종을 심다. You hear it often in talk about home vegetable gardens.

examples.en: This museum has many old works of art.
My uncle's hobby is collecting artworks.
Please look at the artworks with your eyes only, without touching.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 해외로 미술품을 운반하는 일을 해요.
examples.en: That company handles shipping artworks overseas.
I heard a thief stole artworks from the exhibition hall.

examples.ko: 비싼 미술품 앞에서 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos in front of expensive artworks.

explain: '미술품'은 그림, 조각처럼 눈으로 보고 즐기는 작품 전체를 부르는 말이에요. 그림 하나만 말할 때는 '그림'이나 '작품'을 쓰는 게 더 자연스러워요. '작품'은 미술뿐 아니라 책, 영화에도 써요.
explain_en: 미술품 is a broad term for pieces you enjoy by looking, such as paintings and sculptures. For a single painting, 그림 or 작품 sounds more natural. 작품 can also be used for books and films, not just art.

examples.en: I saw fireflies for the first time in the countryside on a summer night.
Fireflies glow twinkling in the grass.

examples.ko: 아이들이 손전등 대신 반디 불빛으로 놀았대요.
examples.en: I heard the children played by the light of fireflies instead of a flashlight.

examples.ko: 깨끗한 물가에서만 반디를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see fireflies only near clean water.
I went to a firefly festival and enjoyed the lights.

examples.ko: 요즘은 도시에서 반디가 거의 안 보여요.
examples.en: These days, fireflies are hardly seen in the city.

explain: '반딧불이'가 정확한 곤충 이름이고, '반디'는 그것을 줄인 말이에요. 빛은 '반딧불'이라고 해요. 시골이나 깨끗한 환경을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The exact insect name is 반딧불이, and 반디 is the shortened form. The light it gives off is called 반딧불. It often comes up when talking about the countryside or clean nature.

examples.en: They take emergency calls at the fire station's control room.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 상황실이 하루 종일 바빴어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the control room was busy all day.

examples.ko: 대회 상황실에는 큰 화면이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: The competition's control room has several big screens.
I work in a broadcasting company's control room.

examples.ko: 사고 소식을 들은 직원들이 상황실로 모였어요.
examples.en: The staff who heard about the accident gathered in the control room.
I'll explain the current situation from the control room.

explain: '상황실'은 재난이나 큰 행사처럼 여러 일이 한꺼번에 일어날 때 정보를 모아 판단하는 방이에요. '사무실'은 평소 일하는 곳이고 상황실은 비상 때 움직이는 곳이에요. 뉴스에서 '재난안전상황실'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A 상황실 is a room where information is gathered and decisions are made when many things happen at once, such as a disaster or a big event. A 사무실 is an ordinary workplace, while a 상황실 is active in emergencies. In the news you often see it in terms like 재난안전상황실.

examples.en: I went to the arboretum with my family on the weekend.

examples.ko: 이 수목원에는 사계절 다른 꽃이 피어요.
examples.en: Different flowers bloom here in the arboretum in every season.

examples.ko: 가을에는 단풍이 예쁜 수목원이 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: In autumn, arboretums with beautiful fall leaves are popular.
I took a slow walk inside the arboretum.

examples.ko: 수목원 입장권은 인터넷으로 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy arboretum tickets online.
I observed insects with my child at the arboretum.

explain: '공원'은 쉬고 노는 곳이고, '수목원'은 여러 나무와 식물을 모아 키우며 보여 주는 곳이에요. '식물원'은 주로 온실에서 키우는 식물을 보여 줘요. 발음은 [수모권]처럼 이어서 소리 나요.
explain_en: A 공원 is for resting and playing, while a 수목원 collects and grows many kinds of trees and plants for people to see. A 식물원 mostly shows plants grown in greenhouses. It is pronounced with linking, like [수모권].

examples.en: This coat has a soft lining, so it is warm.
The lining was torn, so I took it for repair.

examples.ko: 겨울 재킷은 안감에 털이 달린 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For winter jackets, ones with fur lining are good.
A summer suit stays cool if the lining is thin.
The lining color differs from the outer fabric, which looks stylish.
I wrote my name on the inside lining of the jacket.

explain: '안감'은 옷 안쪽에 대는 천이고, 겉에 보이는 천은 '겉감'이에요. 둘은 짝말이라 같이 외우면 좋아요. 발음은 [안깜]처럼 'ㄱ'이 세게 나요.
explain_en: 안감 is the fabric on the inside of clothing, and the fabric you see on the outside is 겉감. They are a pair, so it helps to learn them together. It is pronounced with a tense sound, like [안깜].

examples.ko: 저는 오래된 영화를 좋아하는 영화 애호가예요.
examples.en: I'm a film buff who loves old movies.

examples.ko: 커피 애호가들이 이 가게를 많이 찾아요.
examples.en: Many coffee enthusiasts visit this shop.
A concert for classical music lovers is being held.
He is known as a tea enthusiast.

examples.ko: 책 애호가라면 이 서점을 좋아할 거예요.
examples.en: If you love books, you will like this bookstore.
I went to a photography enthusiasts' meeting for the first time.

explain: '애호가'는 어떤 취미나 분야를 오래 깊이 좋아하는 사람이에요. '팬'은 특정 사람이나 팀을 좋아할 때, 애호가는 영화, 커피, 음악 같은 분야를 좋아할 때 자주 써요. '전문가'는 일로 잘 아는 사람이라 달라요.
explain_en: An 애호가 is someone who deeply loves a hobby or field over a long time. 팬 is usually for a specific person or team, while 애호가 fits fields like film, coffee or music. A 전문가 is someone who knows a field professionally, which is different.

en: a whole lot; in great quantity

examples.en: It was a sale, so I bought a whole lot of clothes.

examples.ko: 어제 비가 왕창 와서 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained heavily yesterday, so the roads were jammed.
Mom made a huge amount of kimchi.
On payday, I treated my friends to a big meal.

examples.ko: 오늘 손님이 왕창 와서 정신이 없었어요.
examples.en: A whole bunch of customers came today, and it was hectic.
My stocks shot up a lot, so I'm in a good mood!

explain: '많이'보다 한꺼번에 확 많은 양이 생기거나 쓰일 때 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. '사다', '먹다', '오다', '쓰다'처럼 한 번에 많이 하는 동작과 잘 어울려요. 격식 있는 글에는 '매우 많이'를 써요.
explain_en: Compared with 많이, this casual word suggests a large amount arriving or being used all at once. It fits actions done in bulk, like 사다, 먹다, 오다 and 쓰다. In formal writing, use 매우 많이 instead.

examples.en: Today is the solar term when autumn begins.
Korea has twenty-four solar terms.
Grandmother cooks food to match the solar terms.

examples.ko: 동지는 일 년 중 밤이 가장 긴 절기예요.
examples.en: Dongji is the solar term with the longest night of the year.

examples.ko: 절기를 알면 날씨 변화를 미리 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know the solar terms, you can anticipate weather changes.
By the solar calendar it's spring, but it is still cold.

explain: '절기'는 한 해를 24개로 나눈 옛 달력의 계절 구분이에요. 입춘, 하지, 동지처럼 날씨와 농사에 쓰였어요. 요즘도 '절기상으로는 봄인데'처럼 날씨 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 절기 is the old calendar's way of dividing the year into 24 seasonal points, such as 입춘, 하지 and 동지, used for weather and farming. Today you still hear it in weather talk, like 절기상으로는 봄인데.

examples.en: The highway on-ramp was blocked, so I was late.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트 진입로는 좁아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The access road to our apartment is narrow, so you need to be careful.
They closed the access road for a while because of construction.
Flowers are in full bloom along the park's entrance road.
A car slowly came in on the access road.
I heard they spread de-icer on the access road because of the snow.

explain: '진입로'는 큰길이나 고속도로, 건물로 들어가는 길이에요. '출구'는 나오는 곳, 진입로는 들어가는 곳으로 짝을 이뤄요. 교통 방송에서는 '진입로가 정체예요'처럼 자주 들려요.
explain_en: A 진입로 is the road you use to enter a main road, highway or building. It pairs with 출구, which is the way out. In traffic reports you often hear phrases like 진입로가 정체예요.

examples.en: After showering, I dried my body with a towel.
The hotel brought me a fresh towel.
When I work out, I wrap a towel around my neck.
Can I borrow a towel at the pool?

examples.ko: 이 타월은 부드럽고 물을 잘 빨아들여요.
examples.en: This towel is soft and absorbs water well.
I hung the wet towel out in the sun.

explain: 집에서는 보통 '수건'이라고 하고, '타월'은 호텔, 수영장, 운동 용품에서 자주 써요. 둘 다 같은 물건이지만 '타월'은 외래어라 조금 더 상품 이름 느낌이에요. 목욕탕의 '때수건'은 '이태리타월'이라고도 불러요.
explain_en: At home people usually say 수건, while 타월 is more common for hotels, pools and sports goods. They refer to the same item, but 타월 is a loanword and feels a bit more like a product name. The scrubbing cloth in a bathhouse is called 이태리타월.

examples.en: The national team's warm-up match is held before the World Cup.
Our team won 2-1 in today's warm-up match.

examples.ko: 감독은 평가전을 통해 선수들의 상태를 확인했어요.
examples.en: The coach checked the players' condition through the warm-up match.

examples.ko: 주말에 평가전을 보러 경기장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to the stadium to watch the warm-up match this weekend.
The warm-up results were good, so my expectations are high.
The warm-up match was canceled because of rain.

explain: '평가전'은 큰 대회 전에 실력과 전술을 시험해 보는 경기예요. 순위에 영향이 큰 '본선'이나 '정규 경기'와 달라서 결과보다 준비 과정이 중요해요. 축구, 야구 같은 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A 평가전 is a match played before a major tournament to test form and tactics. Unlike a 본선 or a regular league match, the result matters less than the preparation. It appears often in sports news for soccer and baseball.

examples.en: A scarecrow stands in the middle of the rice field.
The farmer put up a scarecrow to scare away birds.

examples.ko: 아이들이 허수아비 옷을 입고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The kids put on scarecrow outfits and took photos.

examples.ko: 허수아비 인형이 가을 축제 분위기를 살려요.
examples.en: A scarecrow doll adds to the autumn festival mood.
These days, it has become hard to see scarecrows.

examples.ko: 허수아비처럼 가만히 서 있지만 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand still like a scarecrow; help me.

explain: '허수아비'는 논밭에서 새를 쫓으려고 세우는 사람 모양 인형이에요. 말로는 '진짜 힘이 없는 사람'을 놀릴 때도 써요. 가을 들판 풍경과 같이 떠올리는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사장님은 이름만 있을 뿐 허수아비 같아요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로만 자리에 있고 실제 힘이나 결정권이 없는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who holds a position in name only, without real power or authority.

explain_en: A 허수아비 is a human-shaped figure set up in fields to scare away birds. It can also be used for a person who has no real power. Koreans often picture it in an autumn rice field.

examples.en: Housekeepers often appear in old dramas.

examples.ko: 그 부잣집에는 가정부 두 명이 일해요.
examples.en: Two housekeepers work in that wealthy household.
I saw an advertisement looking for a housekeeper.

examples.ko: 영화 속 가정부는 사실 비밀을 알고 있었어요.
examples.en: The housekeeper in the movie actually knew a secret.
A housekeeper who came from abroad helps with the housework.
Thanks to the housekeeper, the house is always clean.

explain: 요즘 일상에서는 '가정부'보다 '가사도우미', '도우미 아주머니'라고 더 많이 말해요. 가정부는 드라마나 영화에서 자주 들리는 오래된 느낌의 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '이모님'처럼 존중하는 호칭을 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people now more often say 가사도우미 or 도우미 아주머니 than 가정부. 가정부 sounds a bit old-fashioned and shows up mostly in dramas and movies. When speaking to the person directly, a respectful title like 이모님 is used.

examples.en: I put a hook on the wall and hung my bag on it.
The captain is a pirate with a hook for one hand.
The string is caught on the hook and won't come loose.
At the butcher's, meat is hanging from hooks.

examples.ko: 갈고리 모양 손잡이가 달린 지팡이를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a cane with a hook-shaped handle.
The cat's claws are sharp like hooks.

explain: '걸이'나 '고리'는 걸어 두는 물건 전체에 쓰고, '갈고리'는 끝이 굽은 모양을 강조해요. 그래서 물건을 낚거나 매달 때 쓰는 날카로운 쇠붙이에 어울려요. '손'이나 '발톱' 모양을 말할 때도 자주 써요.
explain_en: 걸이 and 고리 are general words for things that hold other things, while 갈고리 stresses a bent, pointed end. It suits a sharp metal piece used to catch or hang things. It is also often used to describe the shape of hands or claws.

examples.en: There is a public cemetery on the hill behind the village.
I went to the public cemetery with my family to visit the graves.

examples.ko: 공동묘지 근처에 집을 지으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not build a house near a public cemetery.

examples.ko: 이 공동묘지는 전쟁 때 돌아가신 분들을 모셨어요.
examples.en: This public cemetery holds those who died in the war.
Only a quiet wind blew through the public cemetery.
Grandfather's grave is at the end of the public cemetery.

explain: '공동묘지'는 여러 집안이 함께 쓰는 묘지예요. 한 집안만 쓰는 '선산'이나 '가족묘'와 달라요. 명절이나 추석에 '성묘'를 가는 곳으로도 나와요.
explain_en: A 공동묘지 is a cemetery shared by many families, unlike a 선산 or 가족묘 used by only one family. It also appears as a place people go to for 성묘 during holidays like 추석.

examples.en: Please fill in your name and address on the form.
I wrote the date in the blank.

examples.ko: 신청서에 내용을 기입하는 데 십 분쯤 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took about ten minutes to fill in the details on the application.

examples.ko: 틀리게 기입한 곳은 한 줄로 지우세요.
examples.en: Cross out the parts you entered incorrectly with a single line.

examples.ko: 전화번호를 기입하지 않으면 접수가 안 돼요.
examples.en: If you don't enter your phone number, we can't accept it.
I will write the amount on the receipt.

explain: '쓰다'는 아무 글에나 쓰지만, '기입하다'는 양식의 빈칸에 필요한 내용을 적을 때 써요. 말할 때는 '적다'나 '쓰다'가 더 흔하고, 기입하다는 서류나 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '작성하다'가 있는데 문서 전체를 쓸 때 쓰고, 기입은 한 칸씩 채우는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: 쓰다 works for any writing, but 기입하다 is for entering required details into the blanks of a form. In speech, 적다 or 쓰다 is more common, and 기입하다 mostly appears on documents and notices. 작성하다 is for writing a whole document, while 기입하다 feels like filling one blank at a time.

examples.ko: 그 동굴은 아주 깊숙해서 불빛이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: That cave is so deep that light doesn't reach it.

examples.ko: 서랍이 깊숙해서 물건이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The drawer is deep, so I can't see things well.

examples.ko: 깊숙한 골목 안에 작은 카페가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe deep inside the alley.

examples.ko: 반지는 가방 깊숙한 곳에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put the ring deep inside my bag.
The deeper into the forest you go, the quieter it gets.

examples.ko: 산속 깊숙한 곳에 있던 그 절은 찾기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That temple tucked deep in the mountains was hard to find.

explain: '깊다'는 위에서 아래로 깊이를 말하고, '깊숙하다'는 바깥에서 안쪽으로 멀리 들어간 곳을 말해요. 그래서 서랍, 가방, 산속, 골목처럼 안으로 들어가는 곳에 어울려요. 보통 '깊숙한 곳', '깊숙이'로 써요.
explain_en: 깊다 describes depth from top to bottom, while 깊숙하다 describes a spot that is far inside from the outside. That is why it suits drawers, bags, mountains and alleys. It usually appears as 깊숙한 곳 or 깊숙이.

examples.en: This movie is the director's debut work.
He is an actor who won great popularity from his debut work.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 데뷔작을 다시 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I reread that author's debut work.

examples.ko: 데뷔작이라고 믿기 어려울 만큼 완성도가 높아요.
examples.en: It is polished enough that it's hard to believe it's a debut work.

examples.ko: 가수의 데뷔작인 첫 앨범이 오늘 나왔어요.
examples.en: The singer's first album, a debut work, came out today.

examples.ko: 데뷔작에서 보여 준 매력이 지금도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the charm shown in the debut work.

explain: '데뷔작'은 영화감독, 배우, 작가가 처음 내놓은 작품이에요. '처녀작'이라는 비슷한 말이 있는데, 더 옛날 느낌이라 요즘은 데뷔작을 더 많이 써요. 반대로 마지막 작품은 '유작'이라고 해요.
explain_en: A 데뷔작 is the first work released by a director, actor or writer. 처녀작 is a similar word but sounds older, so 데뷔작 is more common now. The opposite idea, a final work left behind, is 유작.

examples.en: My friend called me out of the blue.
Tears came out of nowhere, and I was flustered.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 뜬금없이 노래를 부르면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are you doing, singing out of the blue in the middle of a meeting?
My younger sibling suddenly suggested going on a trip.
An old song popped into my head out of nowhere.

examples.ko: 그는 뜬금없이 나타나서 선물을 주고 갔어요.
examples.en: He showed up out of nowhere, gave me a gift, and left.

explain: '갑자기'는 단순히 급하게 일어난 일을 말하고, '뜬금없이'는 앞뒤 흐름과 맞지 않아서 어리둥절한 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '뜬금없는 소리', '뜬금없이 왜 그래?'처럼 써요. 대화에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: 갑자기 just means something happened suddenly, while 뜬금없이 adds a feeling of confusion because it does not fit the flow. It is common in phrases like 뜬금없는 소리 or 뜬금없이 왜 그래?. You will hear it a lot in conversation.

examples.ko: 저 두 사람은 얼굴이 닮은 모녀예요.
examples.en: Those two are a mother and daughter with similar faces.
A mother and daughter walk through the market hand in hand.
This drama portrays the love between a mother and daughter.
We went to Jeju Island on a mother-daughter trip.
I hear a mother and daughter can be as comfortable as friends.

examples.ko: 옆집 모녀가 우리 집에 떡을 가져다줬어요.
examples.en: The mother and daughter next door brought rice cakes to our house.

explain: '모녀'는 어머니와 딸 두 사람을 함께 부르는 말이에요. 아버지와 아들은 '부자', 아버지와 딸은 '부녀', 어머니와 아들은 '모자'라고 해요. 한자 말이라 일상 대화에서는 '엄마랑 딸'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 모녀 refers to a mother and daughter together. Father and son is 부자, father and daughter is 부녀, and mother and son is 모자. In casual talk, people often say 엄마랑 딸 instead.

examples.en: Soup with minari in it smells wonderful.

examples.ko: 봄에는 미나리 무침이 입맛을 살려 줘요.
examples.en: In spring, seasoned minari brings back your appetite.
Grandmother grows minari in the paddy.
Minari grows well by the water.

examples.ko: 삼겹살을 미나리와 같이 먹는 게 인기예요.
examples.en: Eating pork belly with minari is popular.

examples.ko: 시장에서 신선한 미나리 한 단을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a bunch of fresh minari at the market.

explain: '미나리'는 물가에서 자라는 향이 강한 채소로 국, 찌개, 무침에 넣어요. 향이 비슷한 '쑥갓'과는 다른 채소예요. 단위는 '단'으로 세요.
explain_en: 미나리 is a strongly scented vegetable that grows by water and goes into soups, stews and seasoned side dishes. It is a different vegetable from 쑥갓, which has a similar aroma. It is counted by the bunch with 단.

examples.en: Our team held the last line of defense.
The line of defense collapsed under the enemy attack.
The coach told the defenders to push up the defensive line.

examples.ko: 마지막 방어선이라 절대 뚫리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's the last line of defense, so it can never be broken through.
As the budget shrank, the defenses grew weaker.
The hospital is the last line of defense against disease.

explain: '방어선'은 군사 이야기에서 적을 막는 선이지만, 축구 같은 스포츠와 일상 비유에도 써요. '방어선을 구축하다', '방어선이 무너지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요. '수비'가 하는 일이라면 '방어선'은 그 위치예요.
explain_en: 방어선 is a line meant to stop an enemy in military talk, but it is also used in sports like soccer and in everyday metaphors. It pairs with set verbs, as in 방어선을 구축하다 and 방어선이 무너지다. 수비 is the act of defending, while 방어선 is the position where it is done.

examples.en: I trembled while watching a scary movie.
I'm so cold my whole body is shaking.
My hands trembled before the presentation.

examples.ko: 아이가 개를 보고 벌벌 떨면서 울었어요.
examples.en: The child saw a dog, shook with fear, and cried.

examples.ko: 선생님 앞에서 벌벌 떨 필요 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to shake in front of the teacher.

examples.ko: 높은 곳에 올라가니까 다리가 벌벌 떨려요!
examples.en: My legs are shaking since I climbed up somewhere high!

explain: '벌벌'은 무섭거나 추워서 몸이 떠는 모양을 말해요. 늘 '떨다', '떨리다'와 함께 쓰고 '벌벌 떨다'가 하나의 덩어리예요. '덜덜'은 추위나 기계에, '부들부들'은 화나거나 힘줄 때 더 어울려요.
explain_en: 벌벌 shows a body shaking from fear or cold, and it is nearly always used with 떨다 or 떨리다 as 벌벌 떨다. 덜덜 fits cold or machines better, and 부들부들 fits anger or strain.

examples.en: Grandfather smiled gently when he saw his grandchild.

examples.ko: 그녀는 대답 대신 빙그레 미소만 지었어요.
examples.en: She answered with only a quiet smile instead of words.
The child smiled softly after being praised.
Everyone smiled warmly at the good news.
The teacher nodded with a gentle smile.
Dad smiled softly while reading the letter.

explain: '빙그레'는 입을 벌리지 않고 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모양이에요. 소리 내어 크게 웃는 '하하'나 '깔깔'과 달라요. '빙그레 웃다', '빙그레 미소를 짓다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: 빙그레 describes a soft smile made without opening the mouth and without sound. It is different from loud laughter like 하하 or 깔깔. It appears in phrases like 빙그레 웃다 and 빙그레 미소를 짓다.

examples.en: I keep a small cactus on my desk.

examples.ko: 선인장은 물을 자주 안 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: A cactus doesn't need to be watered often.
I pricked my finger on a cactus spine.
Big cacti grow in great numbers in the desert.
A yellow flower bloomed on the cactus!

examples.ko: 바쁜 사람에게는 선인장 같은 식물을 추천해요.
examples.en: For busy people, I recommend plants like a cactus.

explain: '선인장'은 줄기에 물을 저장해서 물을 적게 줘도 사는 식물이에요. 잎이나 줄기에 물을 저장하는 식물 전체는 '다육식물'이라고 하고, 선인장은 그중 한 종류예요. '가시'와 함께 자주 말해요.
explain_en: A 선인장 is a plant that stores water in its stem and survives on very little. The broader group of plants that store water in leaves or stems is 다육식물, and 선인장 is one kind of them. It is often mentioned together with 가시 (thorns).

examples.en: The most common surname in Korea is Kim.
Having the same surname doesn't mean you are family.

examples.ko: 할머니가 우리 집안의 성씨 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother told us the story of our family surname.

examples.ko: 결혼해도 한국 여성은 성씨를 바꾸지 않아요.
examples.en: Korean women do not change their surname after marriage.

examples.ko: 외국 이름은 성씨와 이름의 순서가 달라요.
examples.en: Foreign names have a different order of surname and given name.
I was once teased because of my surname.

explain: '성'은 김, 이, 박처럼 이름의 앞부분을 가리키고, '성씨'는 그 성을 높여서 또는 집안을 말할 때 써요. 예를 들어 '성씨가 어떻게 되세요?'는 '성함'보다 성만 정중하게 묻는 말이에요. 한국은 성이 앞, 이름이 뒤에 와요.
explain_en: 성 is the family-name part such as 김, 이 or 박, and 성씨 is a more polite way to refer to it, or to a lineage. For example, 성씨가 어떻게 되세요? politely asks for just the surname. In Korea the family name comes first and the given name after.

examples.en: I slept soundly last night, so I felt refreshed this morning.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차를 마시면 숙면하는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Drinking warm tea helps you sleep soundly.

examples.ko: 밤에 숙면하려면 낮에 커피를 줄여야 해요.
examples.en: To sleep soundly at night, you should cut back on coffee during the day.

examples.ko: 아기가 숙면해서 엄마도 쉴 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The baby slept soundly, so Mom could rest too.
On days I've slept soundly, the morning feels light.

examples.ko: 이 베개는 숙면할 수 있게 도와줘요.
examples.en: This pillow helps you sleep soundly.

explain: '자다'는 그냥 잠드는 일이고, '숙면하다'는 깊이 푹 잘 자는 것을 말해요. 말할 때는 '푹 자다'가 더 자연스럽고, 숙면하다는 건강 기사나 광고에서 자주 나와요. 명사 '숙면'은 '숙면을 취하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 자다 just means to sleep, while 숙면하다 means sleeping deeply and well. In speech 푹 자다 sounds more natural, and 숙면하다 mostly appears in health articles and ads. The noun 숙면 is used as 숙면을 취하다.

examples.en: We grilled and ate meat over a charcoal fire.
At the campsite, I lit the charcoal.
When making soy sauce, people put in charcoal.
Charcoal is used to remove smells.
Charcoal soot got on my hands.
There are also soaps made from charcoal.

explain: '숯'은 나무를 구워 만든 검은 연료이고, 불이 붙은 숯은 '숯불'이라고 해요. 한국 고깃집에서 '숯불구이'가 맛있다고 할 때 자주 나와요. '석탄'은 땅에서 캐는 연료라서 달라요. 발음은 [숟]이라 받침 'ㅊ'이 'ㄷ' 소리로 나요.
explain_en: 숯 is black fuel made by burning wood, and burning charcoal is called 숯불. It comes up when Korean grill restaurants brag about 숯불구이. 석탄 (coal) is dug from the ground, so it's different. It is pronounced [숟], with the final ㅊ sounding like ㄷ.

examples.ko: 아버지는 작년에 회사가 문을 닫아서 실직했어요.
examples.en: My father lost his job last year when the company closed.

examples.ko: 실직하면 한동안 실업 급여를 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you lose your job, you can receive unemployment benefits for a while.
I suddenly lost my job and feel lost.
I introduced a job to my friend who lost his job.
Many people worry about losing their jobs.
After losing my job, I started studying again.

explain: '실직하다'는 일자리를 잃었다는 사실을 말해요. 회사가 그만두라고 한 경우는 '해고되다', 스스로 그만두면 '퇴직하다', '사직하다'라고 해요. 그래서 실직은 이유보다 결과에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: 실직하다 states the fact of having lost a job. If the company dismisses you it is 해고되다, and if you leave on your own it is 퇴직하다 or 사직하다. So 실직하다 focuses on the result rather than the reason.

examples.en: When you're nervous, try taking slow deep breaths.
I took a big deep breath before the presentation.
After exercising, I rested while breathing deeply.
Just taking a deep breath calms the mind.
The teacher told everyone to take a deep breath.
I took a deep breath before entering the exam room and went in.

explain: '숨을 쉬다'가 기본 호흡이라면 '심호흡하다'는 일부러 숨을 깊게 들이쉬고 내쉬는 것이에요. 긴장을 풀거나 마음을 가라앉힐 때 쓰는 말이에요. '숨을 깊이 쉬다'보다 짧고 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 숨을 쉬다 is ordinary breathing, while 심호흡하다 is deliberately breathing in and out deeply. It is used to relax or calm down. It is shorter and more natural than 숨을 깊이 쉬다.

examples.en: When making kimchi, we add salted shrimp.
A plate of salted seafood was set on the table.
Jeot is salty, so I only eat a little.
They sell many kinds of salted seafood at the market.
Grandmother makes her own salted seafood.

examples.ko: 오래 삭힌 젓이 더 깊은 맛이 나요.
examples.en: Seafood fermented for a long time has a deeper flavor.

explain: '젓'은 새우, 멸치, 조개 같은 해산물을 소금에 절여 삭힌 음식이에요. '새우젓', '멸치젓', '명란젓'처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요. 김치를 담글 때 감칠맛을 더하는 양념으로도 자주 쓰여요. 발음은 [젇]이에요.
explain_en: 젓 is seafood such as shrimp, anchovy or shellfish that has been salted and fermented. It attaches to the ingredient name, as in 새우젓, 멸치젓 and 명란젓. It is also often used as a seasoning to add savory depth to kimchi. It is pronounced [젇].

examples.ko: 든든한 지원군이 와 줘서 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: Reliable backup came, and it gave me strength.

examples.ko: 부모님은 늘 저의 가장 큰 지원군이에요.
examples.en: My parents are always my biggest supporters.
A new reinforcement has joined our team.
We requested that reinforcements be sent.
My friends became my backup and cheered me on.
The reinforcements arrived late in the war.

explain: '지원군'은 원래 싸움을 돕는 군대지만 지금은 나를 돕는 든든한 사람을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. '든든한 지원군', '큰 지원군이 되다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 정해져 있어요. '응원'이 마음으로 힘을 주는 거라면 지원군은 실제로 돕는 사람이에요.
explain_en: 지원군 originally meant troops sent to help in a fight, but today it is used more for a dependable person who helps you. It collocates with 든든한 지원군 and 큰 지원군이 되다. 응원 is giving moral support, while a 지원군 is someone who actually helps.

examples.ko: 이불에 진드기가 생기지 않게 자주 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash my blanket often so mites don't develop.
I got bitten by a tick in the mountains and went to the hospital.
House dust mites cause allergies.
I removed a tick from the puppy's body.
I sprayed mite repellent.
Mites are almost invisible to the eye.

explain: '진드기'는 아주 작은 벌레로 이불이나 반려동물, 풀숲에서 피를 빠는 종류도 있어요. 한국에서 '진드기에 물리다'는 야외 활동 뒤에 주의하라는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. '벼룩'은 뛰어다니는 다른 벌레예요.
explain_en: 진드기 is a very small bug, and some kinds live in blankets, on pets or in grass and suck blood. In Korea, 진드기에 물리다 often appears in news warning people to be careful after outdoor activities. 벼룩 (fleas) are different bugs that jump around.

examples.en: The teacher graded the exam papers all night.
I'll grade your homework and return it tomorrow.
The computer grades the answers automatically.
Please take a short break while I grade.
Shall we swap and grade each other's?

examples.ko: 채점한 결과를 보니까 점수가 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Looking at the graded results, my score went up a lot.

explain: '채점하다'는 시험지나 숙제의 정답과 점수를 매기는 일이에요. 누가 하는지에 따라 '선생님이 채점하다', '스스로 채점하다'처럼 주어가 바뀌어요. 점수를 '받다'는 쪽은 학생이고 '채점하다'는 점수를 주는 쪽이에요.
explain_en: 채점하다 means checking answers and assigning a score to an exam or homework. The subject changes by who does it, as in 선생님이 채점하다 and 스스로 채점하다. The student is the one who receives a score, and the one who 채점하다 is the one giving it.

examples.en: I needed cash, so I withdrew money from the ATM.

examples.ko: 통장에서 한 번에 얼마까지 출금할 수 있어요?
examples.en: How much can I withdraw from the account at once?
You can withdraw even without a card, using a phone.
A fee is added when withdrawing.
As soon as my salary comes in, the rent is automatically withdrawn.
How do I get back money that was withdrawn by mistake?

explain: '출금하다'는 은행 계좌에서 돈을 빼는 일이고, 반대로 넣는 건 '입금하다'예요. 현금을 찾을 때는 '돈을 찾다'가 말로 더 자연스러워요. 자동으로 빠져나갈 때는 '출금되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 출금하다 means taking money out of a bank account, and putting money in is 입금하다. In speech, 돈을 찾다 sounds more natural for getting cash. When money is taken automatically, use 출금되다.
